posts.title: How we paint a night sky
posts.excerpt: Not black, never black. Three blues, one pink and a lot of patience.
posts.content:
Ren mixes the night sky in the morning, in three jars: a deep indigo for the top of the page, a softer blue for the middle and a blue with a drop of pink for the line above the hills.

The fireflies come last, as small yellow dots with a pale ring. Children always count them, so we always know exactly how many there are.

posts.title: Reading the dummy book with a class
posts.excerpt: Twenty-four children found three things we had missed in four months.
posts.content:
Before any colour goes down, the pencil dummy of a book goes to a classroom. Nanami reads it aloud and turns the pages slowly; nobody explains the pictures.

This time they asked where the fox had put its boots, why the moon was on the wrong side of the hill and where the little sister went on page twelve. All three are now fixed.

posts.title: June evenings at the studio
posts.excerpt: Lanterns, not torches, and a jar of fireflies that goes back to the river at nine.
posts.content:
On Saturday evenings in June we leave the studio door open from seven. Neighbours come with their children, sit on the floor and leaf through the dummy books while the light goes.

When the first firefly rises from the water, everybody goes quiet and walks down to the bank. The jar on the windowsill goes back to the river at nine.
